key_insight: OCFormer learns a transformation from simple, independent latent-agent dynamics to coupled physical trajectories, enabling near-optimal multi-agent planning for varying start and goal configurations.
engineering_relevance: Amortized inference could accelerate collision-aware robot or drone fleet planning without solving a new high-dimensional optimal control problem for every configuration.
method: Use a transformer to map analytically tractable latent dynamics into interacting physical-agent trajectories.
Train without precomputed trajectories using PMP Hamiltonian ODE residuals and boundary-matching losses.
Enforce agent permutation equivariance through self-attention and adapt to distribution shifts with L-BFGS fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2D and 3D navigation experiments with up to 128 agents, approximately 220 ms inference on unseen boundary configurations, and adaptation to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds.
watch_item: Physics-informed residual minimization alone does not establish hard collision-avoidance guarantees; safety and latency should be validated under deployment conditions.
paper_title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
